title: Add support for combined image and text embeddings using CLIP

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: This feature would be incredibly useful for our work, allowing us to handle everything within Typesense without the need for additional processing. Thank you for considering it!

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@reporter 

How do you combine the separate vectors produced for the image and text fields?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant1 we simply concatenate the two vectors from CLIP, resulting in a 1024-dimensional embedding (512 + 512), which works pretty well for us. Although it would be great to have other options like averaging or summation if possible :)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: How do you query this 1024 dimensional concatenated embedding with a 512-dimensional query embedding? What will be the value of the remaining half of the query vector?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
At this stage, all TS documents have 1024-dimensional embeddings. We then query for similar documents using document ID:
```json
{
"q": "*",
"vector_query": "embedding:([], id: foobar)",
"sort_by": "_vector_distance:asc, newest:desc"
}

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Got it. Have you tried doing the averaging of the image and text vectors? Supporting averaging would help us support both text search queries as well as document ID based similarity search as you have outlined above. With the concatenate approach, we can't support query text because we will only have half the embedding vector. If average works equally well, we can implement that first.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: We haven’t tried the averaging approach yet since we started with concatenating and it worked well. However, I’m happy to test it within the next day to confirm. So far, we keep the CLIP embeddings separate, which allows us to reindex the collection and compare results. I’ll post an update here once it’s done. Thank you!

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant1 We’ve tested averaging the image and text vectors, and the results are very similar. So, we’re all for using this approach in TS by default. Thank you!

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Ok that sounds good and makes it easier to support both query and document based searches. We will kick-off the work shortly and will post an update on this thread.

comments.author: participant1
reporter
comments.body:
@participant1 We tested it, and CLIP embeddings are now working for multiple fields 🎉 Thank you!

Could you please clarify a couple of questions:
1. Will this configuration create embeddings for every document update, even if the 'from' field values haven't changed? It feels that way based on the logs.
2. It seems that it's also possible to create embeddings from more than two 'from' fields, like [image, text, text]? Is this correct?

comments.author: participant2
reporter
comments.body: Thanks @participant2 That sounds great! The only concern is whether the embeddings generation will occur again when the image value isn’t stored in the collection (`store: false`). We observe similar time and CPU usage when updating the same document with identical image and name values. Could you please clarify this for us?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@reporter 

With `store: false`, it's not possible for us to retrieve and compare the field value for the image, so we will have to re-generate embedding.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: @reporter Maybe you can try `index:false` instead of `store:false`, this wil prevent creating an index for the image field, but will persist it on the disk.
